title: Licensed Professional Land Surveyors (PLS) Directory
demand_signal: Validated by active commercial vendor market and clear high-LTV buyer segments. Active vendors selling licensed land surveyor lists: InfoGlobalData ('Land Surveyor Email List'), LakeB2B, BookYourData ('Land Surveyors'), MedicoLeads (niche industry), AverickMedia, FrescoData, Bookyourdata 'Surveyors' SKU. Distinct from our 2026-05-18 'licensed-professional-engineers-pe' brief — PEs and PLSs are licensed by overlapping state engineering/surveying boards but are different professional credentials with different buyers. Surveying equipment is a $7B+ global market and the buyer LTV per surveyor on equipment alone is exceptionally high: a single GNSS rover + total station bundle is $25K-$80K, and software/subscription stacks (Trimble Business Center, Carlson Survey, Leica Infinity, AutoDesk Civil 3D, Bentley OpenRoads) run $2K-$10K/seat/year. NSPS (National Society of Professional Surveyors) reports ~48,000 licensed PLSs in the US — small enough to feel niche but large enough to support a $99 SKU pipeline. All 50 states regulate surveyors via state boards (often combined PE/PLS board), and most maintain public license lookup portals.
target_audience: Surveying equipment OEMs and dealers (Trimble Geospatial, Leica Geosystems/Hexagon, Topcon Positioning Systems, Sokkia, CHC Navigation, SECO Manufacturing, Carlson Software hardware) — equipment sales $25K-$200K per surveyor/crew; surveying and civil engineering software vendors (Trimble Business Center, Carlson Survey, Leica Infinity, AutoDesk Civil 3D, Bentley OpenRoads/OpenSite, MicroSurvey, Topcon MAGNET) — $2K-$10K/seat/year; UAV/drone-for-survey vendors (DJI Enterprise, Wingtra, senseFly, Quantum Systems, Microdrones) — $15K-$80K per drone system plus PPK/RTK base stations; LiDAR scanner vendors (Leica RTC360, Trimble X7, FARO Focus, Riegl) — $30K-$150K capex; civil engineering and AEC recruiting firms (Kimmel & Associates, JMJ Phillip, surveyor-specific recruiters) — PLS placement fees $20K-$45K each; construction GCs and infrastructure firms (DOT prime contractors) recruiting in-house survey crews; geospatial/GIS software (Esri ArcGIS, QGIS commercial plugins) — $1.5K-$5K/seat/year; surveyor E&O insurance brokers (NSPS-endorsed providers, Victor Insurance) — $2K-$10K/year premiums per surveyor; surveying CE/continuing education providers (NSPS, state society courses, online providers like RedVector); land-records and title-search SaaS (DataTree, Landgate) cross-selling.
public_data_sources: State Boards of Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors — public license lookup in all 50 states (many states have combined PE/PLS boards; some states have stand-alone surveying boards)
NCEES (National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying) Records — public lookup for license verification
NSPS state-society affiliate member directories (partial public)
Texas Board of Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors — public roster with downloadable data
California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors, and Geologists — DCA license search
Florida Board of Professional Surveyors and Mappers — MyFloridaLicense public download
BLS Occupational Employment Statistics (SOC 17-1022) for size validation
competitive_landscape: Lightly crowded at the premium tier. InfoGlobalData, LakeB2B, BookYourData, AverickMedia, and a few others sell surveyor lists at $0.10-$0.50/contact or $1.5K-$4K annual subscriptions. No flat-file SKU under $100 exists. The niche is too narrow for B2B aggregators to bother with state-by-state segmentation, which is exactly where we win — surveying equipment dealers are territorial (e.g., Frontier Precision covers MT/ND/SD/WY, Berntsen covers Midwest), and they buy state-by-state lists, not national. DataStructured wedge: $39-$69 per state PLS roster vs. $1,500-$4,000 annual national subscriptions — a Trimble/Leica regional dealer buys 3-5 states and gets exactly the list their reps will call.
monetization_model: State-level CSVs at $39-$69 each. Fields: surveyor full name, license number (PLS or RPLS depending on state), license status, original issue date, current expiration, firm/employer affiliation (where state board publishes it), business address city/state, NCEES record flag (multi-state mobile surveyor indicator). Regional bundles: 'Pacific Northwest PLS Bundle' (WA + OR + ID + MT) at $129, 'Texas + Oil & Gas States' (TX + OK + LA + NM) at $129 — pitched directly to surveying-equipment dealers whose territories map to those regions. National bundle (~48K records) at $249.
estimated_market_size: ~48,000 licensed PLSs nationally (NSPS / BLS combined estimate). ~7,000 surveying firms (NAICS 541370). Equipment buyer LTV per surveyor: $25K-$200K capex one-time plus $5K-$15K/year software and accessories. Recruiting LTV per surveyor: $20K-$45K placement fee. CE LTV: $300-$800/year/surveyor. The narrow size is offset by exceptionally clean buyer-targeting — every Trimble/Leica/Topcon territory rep, every surveyor recruiter, and every UAV-for-survey rep wants exactly this list.
data_freshness_requirement: Annual updates aligned with state board renewal cycles. Most states renew biennially. New license issuance is slow (~1,500-2,000 new PLSs nationally per year, since the FS+PS exam pipeline is small). Low data decay.
compliance_notes: PASS. State board license registries are public per state engineering/surveying practice acts (analogous to PE, CPA, attorney public records). NCEES records are public verification data. NSPS state-society membership data is public where directories are public-facing. No PII beyond what is on the public license. No client data, no project data.
next_steps: Harvest Texas TBPELS public roster (downloadable) as proof-of-concept and first SKU — TX has the largest active PLS count due to oil & gas and infrastructure
Harvest California DCA, Florida MyFloridaLicense, and Colorado DORA (top-4 by PLS count alongside TX)
Build NCEES-record cross-reference to flag multi-state mobile surveyors (high-LTV target for software vendors)
Add firm-affiliation enrichment via state SoS business registry where state board publishes employer field

Launch TX SKU at $49 on Gumroad; outreach to surveying equipment regional dealers (Frontier Precision, Berntsen, Tiger Supplies, SITECH dealers) — they are exactly the buyer who knows the value of a clean state PLS list
researcher_notes: Distinct from the 2026-05-18 PE brief — PEs and PLSs are different licenses with different buyers (PEs buy civil/structural software and engineering tools; PLSs buy surveying instruments, drones, LiDAR, and field-data-collection stacks). The niche is small (48K PLSs vs. 350K+ PEs) but the per-record buyer LTV is exceptional — surveying equipment is high-capex and territorially sold, which is a structural fit for state-level CSVs. Score 7 because (a) the small total size caps national bundle volume, but (b) territorial buyer behavior makes state SKUs uniquely valuable and (c) the absence of any direct competitor at flat-file pricing leaves us with a clean wedge. Engineering is LOW — state boards have well-structured public rosters and several states publish downloadable data.
